purpose: Lock the invariant that every true Deck Search ends with an authoritative shuffle of the searched deck before ordinary resolution continues, preventing a search from giving usable future deck-order knowledge.

applies_to: any future capability whose player-facing rule is a true search of a deck
scope.distinction: Looking at, revealing, or intentionally reordering a bounded top/bottom portion of a deck is not a Deck Search unless the structured rule explicitly invokes search.deck. Those mechanics preserve their own ordering semantics and shuffle only when their rule explicitly requires it.

resolution_order: authoritative server validates that the effect is a legal Deck Search
server computes eligible search results without exposing source deck-position metadata the player does not need
player makes the permitted private selection
selected card or cards move to the structured destination when the effect says they leave the deck
canonical server-side Shuffle/Randomization owner shuffles the searched deck
only after the shuffle completes may later unrelated effects, listeners or ordinary play resume
ordering_exception_rule: If a future effect intentionally requires a selected card to become a known top/bottom card after the search, the structured sequence must say so explicitly: search/select, shuffle the searched deck, then perform the explicit post-shuffle top/bottom placement. A Deck Search may not silently preserve the pre-search order.

owner_boundaries.Search: validates and resolves the search requirement and eligible set
owner_boundaries.Hidden Information: controls which card identities/information the searching player may see and what the opponent may see
owner_boundaries.Card-Zone: owns movement of selected cards between deck and destination zones
owner_boundaries.Shuffle_Randomization: owns the mandatory post-search shuffle and deterministic test seeding
owner_boundaries.rule: Do not create a card-specific helper or duplicate search/shuffle engine for this invariant.

minimum_acceptance_tests: successful one-card Deck Search shuffles after selected card moves
successful multi-card Deck Search shuffles exactly once after all selected cards move
optional Deck Search that accesses the deck but selects zero still shuffles
Deck Search to hand preserves hidden-information boundaries then shuffles
Deck Search followed by another effect cannot observe the pre-search deck order
look/reveal top N does not auto-shuffle when no search.deck rule exists
explicit top/bottom reorder does not auto-shuffle unless its own rule says so
server-side shuffle is deterministic under test seed and non-client-authoritative in production
